newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-firm - private.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-firm - private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Tuesday were seen steady to firm, possibly $0.50 per cwt higher on light marketings, livestock dealers said.

Marketings on Monday were limited by farmers holding hogs back in anticipation of higher prices, sources said. That optimism was further fueled by sharply higher to limit gains in CME pork complex futures Monday in reponse to the release Friday of USDA's Hogs and Pigs Report, they said.

Most lean hog and all pork belly futures soared to daily trading limits on Monday following the USDA data which showed farmers held fewer hogs back for breeding than the industry had anticipated. Also, although the U.S. hog supply on June 1 was up two percent from a year earlier, the number was less than many industry watchers expected.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to the plant were seen steady at $61.50, livestock dealers said. Illinois top hog prices at plants could range $60.50 to $61.00 and Indiana/Ohio top prices at the plant were seen at $61.00, sources in those areas said.
Hog price strength was seen tempered by light pork demand going into the Independence Day holiday on Friday, they said.

Fresh ham prices near midday were quoted by USDA steady to $2.00 per cwt lower, bellies $2.00 higher in a light test and lean trimmings were $1.00 lower in slow trading. Seventeen loads of pork and six loads of trimmed/processed pork sold.
